newsitem.title: FRANCE: Nearby loadings prop up French wheat prices.
newsitem.headline: Nearby loadings prop up French wheat prices.

text.p: French wheat prices held their ground on Monday despite a new export warning by Guy Legras of the European Union, as markets focused on short-term loading requirements, traders said.
Legras, agriculture director at the European Commission, said on Monday that remarks he had made on Friday pointing towards an imminent EU export slowdown were "reasonable".
Exporters could not expect a "free ride" at the EU's weekly export auction each Thursday, he said.
"These are certainly not bullish remarks but there are still some needs to cover," said one French operator on Monday.
Rouen-delivered wheat was bid at 860 francs per tonne for December and 855 francs for January, traders said.
February was bid at 845 francs and March at 840 francs.
Exporters have expressed scepticism about Legras' original comments, saying the EU has every reason to sell from its large crop now that buyers are around and Argentine competition is cooling off.
They also point out the EU has no tenders for two weeks over Christmas and the New Year.
But some French traders saw irritation at talk of a squeeze play behind Legras' remarks, noting one firm had taken 300,000 tonnes of EU wheat out of the 477,700 tonnes awarded last week.
"Brussels fears there's one person who's trying to corner (the market)," said one trader.
Legras said on Friday that what he called "a few wise guys" were trying to play games with the EU tender bids last week.
But traders said that even if Legras did mean to discourage unusual antics in the wheat market, this may not necessarily mean less wheat for export as a whole.
"It doesn't mean that bids which are better distributed will not be accepted," a French operator said.
Barley and maize were both quiet and unchanged from Friday.
January-March feed barley for Rouen delivery was bid at 845 francs a tonne.
Fob Bordeaux maize was offered at 890 francs a tonne for the same period, having gained five francs on Friday when a trade was done at 885 francs.
All French cash grain prices are quoted on a "July" basis, excluding twice-monthly storage increments of 3.64 francs.
These must be added for every half month that elapses between August 1, 1996, and the loading period in question.
Matif French wheat futures were barely active on Monday, February losing one franc to 881 francs a tonne in volume of five lots. --Paris newsroom +331 4221 5146
